newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: GERMANY UNVEILS PLANS FOR LAARBRUCH AIRBASE.
newsitem.headline: GERMANY UNVEILS PLANS FOR LAARBRUCH AIRBASE.

text.p: German Transport Minister Matthias Wissmann said on Friday he was seeking talks with the Dutch government on the future of Laarbruch, a British airforce base on the German/Dutch border.
Wissmann wants the 650-hectare base, which the British are due to leave by end-1999, turned into a civilian airport.
The German initiative would see the base turned into an "industrial airport" creating an airfreight hub, where logistics firms and manufacturers would also be based.

Wissmann said in a statement that Laarbruch had great potential and significant economic importance and he hoped the Dutch would support the project because of the boost it would give to the regional economies in Germany and the Netherlands.

The Dutch transport ministry has expressed concern about noise levels generated by any civilian development. There are also Dutch concerns that the development would bring a serious safety risk to jets deployed at a neighbouring airfield where the Dutch Royal Airforce has a base.
Wissmann said he hoped to discuss the issue with the Dutch at the next meeting of European Union transport ministers.
